steps.body: Three landmarks fall out of the equations. **Time to peak**: set the vertical velocity v_y − g t = 0, so t_peak = v_y/g. **Max height**: y at that time. **Flight time** (level ground): double the peak time, since the arc is symmetric. Then **range** = vₓ · (flight time).

widget.prompt: With v_y = 20 m/s and g = 10, when does the ball reach its peak? (In seconds.)

commonErrors.feedback: 10 = v_y − g, wrong operation. t_peak = v_y/g = 20/10 = 2 s.
0.5 = g/v_y inverts the ratio. t_peak = v_y/g = 2 s.

explanationVariants: The peak height is v_y²/(2g) = 400/20 = 20 m — same answer, one step.

widget.prompt: Continuing (v_y = 20, g = 10), what is the maximum height? (In meters.)

commonErrors.feedback: 40 = v_y·t_peak ignores the fall term. Max height = 40 − 20 = 20 m.

steps.body: Because the up-and-down path is symmetric, the ball spends as long falling as rising: **flight time = 2·t_peak**. During that whole time the horizontal motion never pauses, so the **range** = vₓ · (flight time) — the horizontal reach at landing.

explanationVariants: Rising 2 s, falling 2 s: 4 s aloft.

widget.prompt: With t_peak = 2 s, what is the total flight time on level ground? (In seconds.)

commonErrors.feedback: 2 s is only the RISING half. Double it for the full flight: 4 s.

explanationVariants: Range = vₓ · flight time = 15·4 = 60 m — where the ball lands.
Horizontal speed 15 for the full 4 s covers 60 m.

widget.prompt: With vₓ = 15 m/s and flight time 4 s, what is the range? (In meters.)

commonErrors.feedback: 30 = vₓ·t_peak uses only half the flight. Range uses the FULL 4 s: 15·4 = 60 m.
19 = 15 + 4 adds. Range is a product: 15·4 = 60 m.

explanationVariants: v_y = 30, g = 10: t_peak = 3 s, flight = 6 s. With vₓ = 8, range = 8·6 = 48 m.
Peak at 3 s, aloft 6 s, horizontal 8 m/s → 48 m.

widget.prompt: A ball has vₓ = 8 m/s, v_y = 30 m/s, g = 10. Find its range in meters.

commonErrors.feedback: 24 = vₓ·t_peak uses half the flight. Full flight is 6 s: 8·6 = 48 m.
240 = vₓ·v_y mixes speeds. Range = vₓ·flight time = 8·6 = 48 m.

takeaways: Time to peak = v_y/g; max height = v_y²/(2g).
Flight time = 2·t_peak (level ground); range = vₓ · flight time.
Symmetry makes the fall mirror the rise.
steps.teaser: Finale: erase t to reveal the parabolic path itself.

concept.body: t_peak = v_y/g; max height = value of y there; flight time = 2·t_peak; range = vₓ · flight time.

explanationVariants: Divide the vertical speed by g: 4 s.

widget.prompt: v_y = 40 m/s, g = 10. Find the time to peak (seconds).

commonErrors.feedback: 30 = v_y − g subtracts. Use the ratio v_y/g = 4 s.
